q.t: Which instrument is used to draw arcs and circles?
q.e: A compass keeps its opening fixed, so every point it marks is the same distance from the needle point.

q.t: Which instrument measures angles?
q.e: A protractor is marked in degrees from 0° to 180°.

q.t: Can a triangle be constructed with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm?
q.e: The arcs of 3 cm and 4 cm drawn from the ends of the 8 cm side are too short to meet.

q.t: A triangle is constructed from three given sides. Which rule guarantees it is the only possible triangle?
q.e: Three side lengths fix a triangle completely, so everyone’s drawing is congruent.

q.t: To construct a 60° angle with a compass, we use the idea of:
q.e: Arcs of the same radius from two points make three equal distances — an equilateral triangle, whose angles are 60°.

q.t: The line that cuts a segment into two equal parts at 90° is its:
q.e: Perpendicular = at 90°; bisector = cuts into two equal parts.

q.t: Bisecting a 60° angle gives an angle of:
q.e: Bisect means cut into two equal halves: 60 ÷ 2 = 30.

q.t: How many different triangles can be made with sides 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm (not counting flips and turns)?
q.e: By SSS, any two triangles with these sides are congruent, so there is really only one.

q.t: To draw a line parallel to a given line through a point outside it, we copy an angle so that:
q.e: Equal alternate or corresponding angles force two lines to be parallel.

q.t: A triangle is to be drawn given two sides and the angle between them. This uses the rule:
q.e: Side, included Angle, Side — draw one side, make the angle at its end, then mark the second side along the new arm.

q.t: Can a triangle be constructed with angles 60°, 70° and 60°?
o: No, because they add up to 190°
No, because two angles are equal
q.e: The angles of every triangle must add to exactly 180°.

q.t: To construct a right-angled triangle by RHS you need the hypotenuse and:
q.e: RHS = Right angle, Hypotenuse, Side.

q.t: A 45° angle is constructed by bisecting an angle of:
q.e: Half of 90° is 45°. So first construct a right angle, then bisect it.

q.t: Stepping off the radius on an arc twice from the starting arm gives an angle of:
q.e: Each step of the radius along the arc marks 60°, so two steps give 120°.

q.t: In △ABC, AB = 5 cm, ∠A = 50° and ∠B = 60°. Find ∠C (in degrees).
q.e: 180 − 50 − 60 = 70. (This triangle is drawn using ASA.)

q.t: Can a triangle be constructed with sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 10 cm?
o: No, because two sides are equal
q.e: The two 5 cm sides would lie flat along the 10 cm side — no height, so no triangle. The sum must be strictly greater.

q.t: How many lines can be drawn through a point P parallel to a line l that does not pass through P?
q.e: Only one direction keeps the same distance from l all the way, so there is exactly one such line.

q.t: △PQR is constructed with PQ = 6 cm, QR = 8 cm and ∠Q = 90°. What will PR measure (in cm)?
q.e: PR is the hypotenuse: 6² + 8² = 100, so PR = 10 cm. A good way to check your drawing.

q.t: A 75° angle can be constructed by bisecting the angle between:
q.e: 75 is halfway between 60 and 90, so bisect the 30° gap between those two arms.

q.t: To draw a parallel through point P, an angle of 65° is copied at P as an alternate angle. The lines are parallel because:
o: Equal alternate angles mean parallel lines
q.e: If a transversal makes equal alternate angles with two lines, the lines cannot meet.

q.t: To construct △ABC with all three sides given, which comes right after drawing the base BC?
o: Draw arcs from B and C with radii equal to the other two sides
Measure an angle at B with a protractor
q.e: A is the point that is the correct distance from B and from C — exactly where the two arcs cross.

q.t: Can a triangle be constructed with a 6 cm side whose two end angles are 105° and 80°?
o: No, because 105 + 80 is already more than 180
No, because 6 cm is too short
q.e: The two arms would spread apart and never meet — the third angle would have to be negative.

q.t: The perpendicular distance between two parallel lines is:
q.e: That is what parallel means — the lines never get closer or further apart.

q.t: A right-angled triangle is constructed with hypotenuse 13 cm and one side 5 cm. Find the third side (in cm).
q.e: 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144, so the third side is 12 cm.

q.t: △ABC is constructed with BC = 6 cm, ∠B = 60° and ∠C = 60°. What will AB measure (in cm)?
q.e: The third angle is also 60°, so the triangle is equilateral and every side is 6 cm.

q.t: Which of these angles CANNOT be constructed with ruler and compass alone (using 60°, 90° and bisecting)?
q.e: 15 = 60 ÷ 4, 22.5 = 90 ÷ 4 and 75 = 60 + 15 all come from 60°, 90° and halving. 40° does not.

q.t: You must construct △ABC with AB = 7 cm, ∠A = 45° and ∠C = 75°. What should you find first?
q.e: ASA needs the angles at BOTH ends of the known side AB. ∠B = 180 − 45 − 75 = 60°.

q.t: An isosceles triangle is constructed with base 6 cm and equal sides 5 cm. What will its height be (in cm)?
q.e: The height bisects the base into 3 cm and 3 cm, making a right triangle: 5² − 3² = 16, so the height is 4 cm.

q.t: How many different triangles can be made with sides 4 cm and 6 cm and an angle of 50° between them?
q.e: SAS fixes the triangle completely — only one.

q.t: How many lines are there parallel to a line l at a distance of 3 cm from it?
q.e: One on each side of l.

q.t: How many different triangles have whole-number sides (in cm) and a perimeter of 12 cm?
q.k: len([(a,b,c) for a in range(1,12) for b in range(a,12) for c in range(b,12) if a+b+c==12 and a+b>c])
q.e: List them with the longest side less than 6 (half the perimeter): (2, 5, 5), (3, 4, 5) and (4, 4, 4).

q.t: Given two sides and an angle that is NOT between them, how many different triangles might be possible?
q.e: The side opposite the given angle can swing like a door and may touch the base line in two places. That is why SSA is not a congruence rule.

q.t: Which pair of constructions gives a 105° angle?
q.e: 90 + 15 = 105, and 15° comes from bisecting 60° twice. (The others give 90°, 60° and 90°.)

q.t: △ABC has ∠B = 90°, BC = 5 cm and AB + AC = 25 cm. Find AB (in cm).
q.e: Let AB = x, so AC = 25 − x. Pythagoras: (25 − x)² = x² + 25 → 625 − 50x = 25 → x = 12. (Then AC = 13: the 5-12-13 triangle.)

q.t: A triangle has sides a, a + 1 and a + 2 cm and perimeter 24 cm. Find its longest side (in cm).
q.e: 3a + 3 = 24, so a = 7. Sides 7, 8, 9 — and 7 + 8 > 9, so the triangle can be drawn.

q.t: Two sides of a triangle are 7 cm and 12 cm. How many whole-number lengths (in cm) can the third side have?
q.k: len([c for c in range(1,40) if 12-7<c<12+7])
q.e: It must be more than 12 − 7 = 5 and less than 12 + 7 = 19: the values 6 to 18, which is 13 numbers.

q.t: A right angle is bisected, and one half is bisected again. What is the size of the smallest angle made (in degrees)?
q.e: 90 → 45 → 22.5. Each bisection halves the angle.

q.t: To construct the perpendicular bisector of a 10 cm segment, the compass opening must be:
q.e: The arcs from the two ends must cross. With 5 cm or less they only just touch or miss; more than half the length makes them cross above and below.

q.t: Which set of measurements does NOT fix one unique triangle?
o: Sides 5 cm and 6 cm with 60° between them
A 6 cm side with angles 50° and 60° at its ends
q.e: Three angles give the shape but not the size — you could draw it as big or as small as you like.

q.t: A parallel line is drawn using a corresponding angle of 65°. What is the co-interior angle on the new line (in degrees)?
q.e: Co-interior angles on parallel lines add to 180°: 180 − 65 = 115.
